pages.label: Page 6
pages.title: The Triumph of the Name of Jesus — Giovanni Battista Gaulli

pages.label: Page 7
pages.title: In the Beginning
pages.text:
JOHN 1:1, 3-5, 11-12, 14

In the Beginning

In the beginning was the Word, and the Word
was with God, and the Word was God.
All things were made through him. Without
him, nothing was made that has been made.
In him was life, and the life was the light of
men. The light shines in the darkness, and the
darkness has not overcome it.
He came to his own people, but they did not
receive him. But to all who did receive him, and
believed in his name, to them he gave the right
to become children of God.
And the Word became flesh and dwelt among
us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the only
Son of the Father, full of grace and truth.

Giovanni Battista Gaulli
The Triumph of the Name of Jesus, 1676–1679 7
Chiesa del Gesù, Rome

pages.label: Page 8
pages.title: The Annunciation
pages.text:
LU K E 1 : 2 6 - 2 9

The Annunciation

In the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was
sent from God to a city of Galilee named
Nazareth, to a virgin pledged to be married
to a man whose name was Joseph, of
David’s house. The virgin’s name was Mary.
Having come in, the angel said to her,
“Greetings, you who are full of grace! The
Lord is with you. Blessed are you among
women!”
But when she saw him, she was greatly
troubled at the saying and considered what
kind of greeting this might be.

Sandro Botticelli
8 The Cestello Annunciation, 1489–1490
Gallerie degli Uffizi, Florence

pages.label: Page 10
pages.title: Annunciation with Saints — Simone Martini and Lippo Memmi

pages.label: Page 11
pages.title: Do Not Be Afraid
pages.text:
LU K E 1 : 3 0 - 3 4

Do Not Be Afraid

The angel said to her, “Do not be
afraid, Mary, for you have found
favor with God. Behold, you will conceive
in your womb and give birth to a son and
shall name him ‘Jesus.’ He will be great
and will be called the Son of the Most
High. The Lord God will give him the
throne of his father David, and he will
reign over the house of Jacob forever, and
his kingdom will have no end.”
Mary said to the angel, “How can this be
since I am a virgin?”

Simone Martini and Lippo Memmi
Annunciation with Saints, 1333 11
Gallerie degli Uffizi, Florence

pages.label: Page 12
pages.title: Let It Be Done
pages.text:
LU K E 1 : 3 5 - 3 8

Let It Be Done

The angel answered her, “The Holy
Spirit will come on you, and the
power of the Most High will overshadow
you. Therefore also the holy one who is
born from you will be called the Son of
God. Behold, Elizabeth your relative also
has conceived a son in her old age; and
this is the sixth month with her who was
called barren. For nothing is impossible
with God.”
Mary said, “Behold, I am the servant of
the Lord; let it be done to me according to
your word.” Then the angel departed from
her.

Henry Ossawa Tanner
12 The Annunciation, 1898
Philadelphia Museum of Art

pages.label: Page 14
pages.title: The Dream of Saint Joseph — Philippe de Champaigne

pages.label: Page 15
pages.title: The Dream of Joseph
pages.text:
M AT T H E W 1 : 1 8 - 2 1

The Dream of Joseph

Now the birth of Jesus Christ was like this:
After his mother, Mary, was engaged to
Joseph, before they came together, she was found
to be with child by the Holy Spirit. Her husband
Joseph, being a just man and not willing to put her
to shame, decided to divorce her quietly.
But when he thought about these things, behold,
an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream,
saying, “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to
take to yourself Mary as your wife, for that which is
conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.
“She shall give birth to a son. You shall name him
Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.”

Philippe de Champaigne
The Dream of Saint Joseph, 1642–1643 15
The National Gallery, London

pages.label: Page 16
pages.title: Call Him Immanuel
pages.text:
M AT T H E W 1 : 2 2 - 2 5

Call Him Immanuel

Now all this has happened that it
might be fulfilled which was spoken
by the Lord through the prophet, saying,
“Behold, the virgin shall be with child,
and shall give birth to a son. They shall
call him Immanuel,” which means, “God
with us.”
Joseph arose from his sleep and did as
the angel of the Lord commanded him
and took his wife to himself; and didn’t
know her until she had given birth to her
firstborn son.

Raphael
16 The Marriage of the Virgin, 1504
Pinacoteca di Brera, Milan

pages.label: Page 17
pages.title: The Marriage of the Virgin — Raphael

pages.label: Page 19
pages.title: The Visitation
pages.text:
LU K E 1 : 3 9 - 4 5

The Visitation

Mary arose in those days and went
into the hill country with haste, into
a city of Judah, and entered into the house
of Zacharias and greeted Elizabeth. When
Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby
leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was
filled with the Holy Spirit.
She called out with a loud voice and said,
“Blessed are you among women, and blessed
is the fruit of your womb! Why am I so
favored, that the mother of my Lord should
come to me? For behold, when the voice of
your greeting came into my ears, the baby
leaped in my womb for joy! Blessed is she
who believed, for there will be a fulfillment
of the things which have been spoken to her
from the Lord!”

Domenico Ghirlandaio
The Visitation, 1491 19
Musée du Louvre, Paris

pages.label: Page 20
pages.title: My Soul Magnifies the Lord
pages.text:
LU K E 1 : 4 6 - 5 5

My Soul Magnifies
the Lord
Mary said, “My soul magnifies the Lord! My
spirit rejoices in God my Savior, for he has
looked at the humble state of his servant. From
now on, all generations will call me blessed.
“For he who is mighty has done great things for
me. Holy is his name. His mercy is for generations
and generations on those who fear him.
“He has shown strength with his arm. He has
scattered the proud in the imagination of their
hearts. He has put down princes from their
thrones, and has exalted the lowly. He has filled
the hungry with good things. He has sent the
rich away empty. He has given help to Israel,
his servant, that he might remember mercy, as
he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and his
offspring forever.”

Titian
20 Assumption of the Virgin, 1516–1518
Basilica di Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari, Venice

pages.label: Page 22
pages.title: The Age of Augustus, the Birth of Christ — Jean-Léon Gérôme

pages.label: Page 23
pages.title: Everyone to His Own City
pages.text:
LU K E 2 : 1 - 5

Everyone to His
Own City

Now in those days, a decree went out
from Caesar Augustus that all the
world should be registered. This was the
first census made when Quirinius was
governor of Syria.
All went to register themselves, everyone
to his own city. Joseph also went up from
Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into
Judea, to David’s city Bethlehem, because
he was of the house and family of David, to
enroll himself with Mary, who was pledged
to be married to him and was with child.

Jean-Léon Gérôme
The Age of Augustus, the Birth of Christ, c. 1852–1854 23
J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles

pages.label: Page 24
pages.title: The Birth of Christ
pages.text:
LU K E 2 : 6 - 7

The Birth of Christ

While they were there, the day had
come for her to give birth. She gave
birth to her firstborn son.
She wrapped him in swaddling clothes and
laid him in a manger, because there was no
room for them in the inn.

Carlo Maratta
24 The Holy Night, c. 1656
Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden

pages.label: Page 26
pages.title: The Angel Appearing to the Shepherds — Thomas Cole

pages.label: Page 27
pages.title: Glory to God
pages.text:
LU K E 2 : 8 - 1 4

Glory to God

There were shepherds in the same country staying
in the field, and keeping watch by night over
their flock. Behold, an angel of the Lord stood by
them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them,
and they were terrified.
The angel said to them, “Do not be afraid, for behold,
I bring you good news of great joy which will be to
all the people. For there is born to you today, in the
city of David, a Savior who is Christ the Lord. This
is the sign for you: you will find a baby wrapped in
swaddling clothes and lying in a manger.”
Suddenly, there was with the angel a multitude of the
heavenly army praising God and saying, “Glory to God
in the highest! And on earth peace, good will toward
men.”

Thomas Cole
The Angel Appearing to the Shepherds, 1833–1834 27
Chrysler Museum of Art, Norfolk

pages.label: Page 28
pages.title: They Went with Haste
pages.text:
LU K E 2 : 1 5 - 2 0

They Went with Haste

When the angels went away from them
into the sky, the shepherds said to one
another, “Let’s go to Bethlehem, now, and see
this thing that has happened, which the Lord
has made known to us.” They went with haste
and found both Mary and Joseph, and the baby
was lying in the manger.
When they saw it, they told everyone the
saying which was spoken to them about this
child.
All who heard it wondered at the things which
were spoken to them by the shepherds. But
Mary treasured all these things, pondering
them in her heart.
The shepherds returned glorifying and praising
God for all the things that they had heard and
seen, just as it was told them.

Gerrit van Honthorst
28 The Adoration of the Shepherds, 1622
Wallraf-Richartz-Museum, Cologne

pages.label: Page 29
pages.title: The Adoration of the Shepherds — Gerrit van Honthorst

pages.label: Page 30
pages.title: Journey of the Magi — James Tissot

pages.label: Page 31
pages.title: Wise Men from the East
pages.text:
M AT T H E W 2 : 1 - 4

Wise Men
from the East
Now when Jesus was born in
Bethlehem of Judea in the days of
King Herod, behold, wise men from the
east came to Jerusalem, saying, “Where is
he who is born King of the Jews? For we
saw his star in the east, and have come to
worship him.”
When King Herod heard it, he was
troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
Gathering together all the chief priests and
scribes of the people, he asked them where
the Christ would be born.

James Tissot
Journey of the Magi, c. 1894 31
Minneapolis Institute of Art

pages.label: Page 32
pages.title: In Bethlehem of Judea
pages.text:
M AT T H E W 2 : 5 - 8

In Bethlehem
of Judea
They said to him, “In Bethlehem of
Judea, for this is written through the
prophet, ‘ You Bethlehem, land of Judah,
are in no way least among the princes of
Judah; for out of you shall come a ruler
who shall shepherd my people, Israel.’ ”
Then Herod secretly called the wise men
and learned from them exactly what
time the star appeared. He sent them to
Bethlehem, and said, “Go and search
diligently for the young child. When you
have found him, bring me word, so that I
also may come and worship him.”

Sandro Botticelli
32 The Adoration of the Magi, ca. 1478/1482
National Gallery of Art, Washington, DC, USA

pages.label: Page 33
pages.title: The Adoration of the Magi — Sandro Botticelli

pages.label: Page 34
pages.title: The Adoration of the Magi — Gentile da Fabriano

pages.label: Page 35
pages.title: Gold, Frankincense, & Myrrh
pages.text:
M AT T H E W 2 : 9 - 1 2

Gold, Frankincense,
& Myrrh
Having heard the king, they went their
way. And behold, the star, which they
saw in the east, went before them until it came
and stood over where the young child was.
When they saw the star, they rejoiced with
exceedingly great joy. They came into the
house and saw the young child with Mary, his
mother, and they fell down and worshiped
him.
Opening their treasures, they offered to him
gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
Being warned in a dream not to return to
Herod, they went back to their own country
another way.

Gentile da Fabriano
The Adoration of the Magi, 1423 35
Gallerie degli Uffizi, Florence

pages.label: Page 36
pages.title: The Presentation
pages.text:
LU K E 2 : 2 1 - 2 2

The Presentation

On the eighth day when he was
circumcised, his name was called
Jesus, which was given by the angel
before he was conceived in the womb.
When the days of their purification
according to the law of Moses were
fulfilled, they brought him up to
Jerusalem to present him to the Lord.

James Tissot
36 Reconstruction of Jerusalem and the Temple of Herod, 1886–1894
Brooklyn Museum, New York

pages.label: Page 37
pages.title: Reconstruction of Jerusalem and the Temple of Herod — James Tissot

pages.label: Page 38
pages.title: The Presentation in the Temple — Philippe de Champaigne

pages.label: Page 39
pages.title: My Eyes Have Seen Your Salvation
pages.text:
LU K E 2 : 2 5 - 3 2

My Eyes Have Seen
Your Salvation

There was a man in Jerusalem whose name was
Simeon. He was righteous and devout, looking for
the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon
him. It had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he
should not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.
He came in the Spirit into the temple. When the parents
brought in the child Jesus, that they might do concerning
him according to the custom of the law, he took him into
his arms and blessed God, and said,
“Lord, now you have released your servant to depart in
peace; for my eyes have seen your salvation, which you
have prepared in the presence of all peoples; a light for
revelation to the nations, and for the glory of your people
Israel.”

Philippe de Champaigne
The Presentation in the Temple, 1648 39
Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium, Brussels

pages.label: Page 40
pages.title: A Sword Will Pierce Your Heart
pages.text:
LU K E 2 : 3 3 - 3 5

A Sword Will Pierce
Your Heart

J oseph and his mother were marveling
at the things which were spoken
concerning him.
Simeon blessed them and said to Mary, his
mother, “Behold, this child is appointed
for the falling and rising of many in Israel,
and for a sign which is spoken against. A
sword will pierce your heart also. And the
thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.”

William-Adolphe Bouguereau
40 The Virgin with Angels, 1900
Petit Palais, Paris

pages.label: Page 41
pages.title: The Virgin with Angels — William-Adolphe Bouguereau

pages.label: Page 43
pages.title: Flight to Egypt
pages.text:
M AT T H E W 2 : 1 3 - 1 5

Flight to Egypt

When they had departed, behold,
an angel of the Lord appeared to
Joseph in a dream, saying, “Arise and take
the young child and his mother and flee
into Egypt and stay there until I tell you,
for Herod will seek the young child to
destroy him.”
He arose and took the young child and his
mother by night and departed into Egypt
and was there until the death of Herod, that
it might be fulfilled which was spoken by
the Lord through the prophet, saying, “Out
of Egypt I have called my son.”

Eugène Girardet
Flight into Egypt 43
Image source: Sotheby’s, 2018, lot 846

pages.label: Page 44
pages.title: A City Called Nazareth
pages.text:
M AT T H E W 2 : 1 9 - 2 3

A City Called Nazareth

When Herod was dead, behold, an angel
of the Lord appeared in a dream to
Joseph in Egypt, saying, “Arise and take the
young child and his mother, and go into
the land of Israel, for those who sought the
young child’s life are dead.”
He arose and took the young child and his
mother and came into the land of Israel.
But when he heard that Archelaus was
reigning over Judea in the place of his father,
Herod, he was afraid to go there.
Being warned in a dream, he withdrew into
the region of Galilee and settled in a city
called Nazareth; that it might be fulfilled
which was spoken through the prophets that
he will be called a Nazarene.

Bartolomé Esteban Murillo
44 The Holy Family with a Little Bird, c. 1650
Museo Nacional del Prado, Madrid

pages.label: Page 45
pages.title: The Holy Family with a Little Bird — Bartolomé Esteban Murillo

pages.label: Page 47
pages.title: In Favor with God and Men
pages.text:
LU K E 2 : 5 1 - 5 2

In Favor with
God and Men

And Jesus went down with them and
came to Nazareth. He was subject to
them, and his mother treasured all these
things in her heart.
And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature,
and in favor with God and men.

Raphael
The Canigiani Holy Family, c. 1505–1506 47
Alte Pinakothek, Munich
